title: Repair the cooking order

samples.expect: [flour; water; salt; dough; tomatoes; sauce; pizza]
samples.label: cooking_order (graph [("pizza", ["dough"; "sauce"]); ("dough", ["flour"; "water"; "salt"]); ("sauce", ["tomatoes"; "salt"])]) "pizza"

hints: Run the pizza test and read the list. Which item comes first, and does anything appear twice?
The item is written down on the way in. Move `order := item :: !order` below the `List.iter`, so it runs after every part has been visited.
Nothing looks in `done_`. Wrap the body of `visit` in `if not (Hashtbl.mem done_ item) then begin ... end`.

answer.explain: `visit` first looks in `done_` and does nothing if the item is already there, so `salt` is written once. Then it marks the item, visits each part, and only after that adds the item to `order`. Writing the item on the way out is what puts every part before the thing that needs it. The list is built backwards with `::` and reversed once at the end.
